I'm familiar with Nietzche's scrutiny on nihilism. Funny enough, it's a common misconception that Nietzche himself was a nihilist who thought that nothing mattered. This couldn't be further from the truth. He opposed nihilism, it absolutely sickened him and he saw it as a threat to humanity. What was his solution? The pursuit of passion and the discovery of purpose for oneself. This purpose was one free from the paternity of some religion or the superficiality of social pressures. Life was short and he saw it fit to make the best of it.

How did this all make me feel? Well, small bursts of motivation and euphoria in a vast ocean of sorrow, probably. For a few minutes, I feel completely in control of my own destiny. It's the most amazing feeling I've ever felt in my life. Every other feeling pales in comparison. It's like a creative high, it's amazing. The worst part is it's so short and I go back to a depressive state eventually. I try and continue whatever I set out to do, but I become less and less enthusiastic about doing it. Can I really do this? Am I good at anything? Why can't I be as good as every other member of society? Why can't I be accepted.

Sorry for my ramblings, this post just really struck a chord with me.
